claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys is influenced by interactions between lattice distortion and dislocation dynamics.
Interactions between lattice distortion and dislocation dynamics enable high-entropy alloys to combine strength and ductility.
The interaction between lattice distortion and dislocation dynamics permits absorption and redistribution of stress.
Stress absorption and redistribution caused by lattice-distortion/dislocation interactions lead to improved strength and ductility.
Under dynamic mechanical loading, high-entropy alloys will exhibit greater strength than conventional-alloy controls.
Under dynamic mechanical loading, high-entropy alloys will exhibit greater ductility than conventional-alloy controls.
High-entropy alloys are predicted to show a 10–20% increase in yield strength relative to the conventional-alloy baseline.
High-entropy alloys are predicted to show a 15–30% increase in ductility relative to the conventional-alloy baseline.
The proposed behavior should hold for alloys containing at least five principal elements.
The proposed behavior should hold when the maximum atomic-radius difference is no more than 20%.
The proposed behavior should hold at strain rates from 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
The proposed behavior should hold at temperatures from -200°C to 500°C.
Failure to observe enhanced strength and ductility relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe a correlation between lattice distortion or dislocation dynamics and mechanical behavior would falsify the hypothesis.
